name: Pediatrician

pf.license.need: always: each pediatrician (MD or DO), nurse practitioner, physician assistant and nurse holds their own active license from the state where the child is during the visit; which roles need which license comes from the state's form (a switch)
pf.license.who: each person; the practice too where the state's form registers medical offices or their owners
pf.license.ask: each person's license number in their invite reply (or the owner sends it); the practice's registration number from the owner
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.video: a video visit only with someone licensed in the state where the child will be during the visit; nobody licensed there: no video times, and an office visit is offered instead
pf.license.away: home visits only where the state's rules allow them, with any home-visit registration the state's form asks for (a switch)
pf.license.lactation: breastfeeding help: the lactation consultant's certification on file; a state license only where the state's form asks for one (a switch)
pf.license.vaccines: shots from the state's free vaccine program only under the practice's own enrollment, where the state's form asks for one (a switch)
pf.license.agreement: a health privacy agreement (a HIPAA business associate agreement) signed on the secure page before the first booking; every company in Rosie's chain signs one with Rosie
pf.license.renewals: optional reminders the owner sets; a license the owner says has lapsed pauses that person's new bookings for that work (the owner's word, never a check)
pf.license.insurance: malpractice insurance where the state's form asks for it
pf.license.claims: 'board-certified' is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie

pf.services.shape: visits with a set length, booked with a pediatrician or a nurse practitioner by name; well-child visits follow the office's own schedule of ages; same-day sick times open each morning; the shots due at a visit are chosen by the clinician there and never paid up front, and a flu shot can also be booked on its own as a nurse visit; a newborn's visit at home has a 2-hour arrival window
pf.services.examples: the example offices' own prices (Lee Family Pediatrics and Lee Newborn Care), not a standard; a plan pays its own in-network fee, and the family's share is an estimate

list.name: Well-child visit (by age, with any shots due)
list.price: billed to the child's plan; self-pay $195
list.length: 30 min (40 min for a new family's first visit)
list.after: any share at the front desk
list.note: booked on the office's schedule of ages; the next one is booked at checkout

list.name: Sick visit (same day)
list.price: billed to the child's plan, any copay at the front desk; self-pay $140
list.after: any copay at the front desk
list.note: same-day times open at 7am, for current patients first; Sam OKs a new family's same-day visit

list.name: Video visit (current patients)
list.price: billed to the child's plan; self-pay $140
list.where: by video, counted as at the office
list.after: any share taken by the front desk, the office's own way
list.note: only while the child is in a state where the clinician is licensed

list.name: Flu shot (nurse visit)
list.price: billed to the child's plan; self-pay $20 for the shot visit
list.before: nothing taken, never paid up front
list.after: any share at the front desk
list.note: a nurse gives it on the clinician's order; often added to another visit

list.name: Sports or school physical
list.price: $40 self-pay, or billed to the plan where it pays
list.where: at the office, or on a school's physicals day

list.after: the office's own way, only with the teen
list.note: only the visit types the office marks private, where the state's rules let a teen consent alone

list.note: in the baby's first days home

list.where: at the family's home, or at the office

list.name: Follow-up weight check at home
list.price: $89; billed to the baby's plan, or self-pay
list.after: as for the newborn home visit

pf.services.capacity: one child per visit; a sibling is added as a second person on the same booking, each with their own time
pf.services.nobodyHome: never: a parent or guardian is always there
pf.services.online: video visits for current patients, counted as at the office, with the check-in code read out at the start

pf.questions.whoMayBook: a parent or legal guardian, or an adult the family's record names; either parent may, unless the office holds a court order that limits it (Rosie follows the record, never the caller's word alone); a teen alone only for the visit types the office marks private, where the state's rules let a minor consent (a switch); a child under 13 never books, and nothing about them is kept

pf.questions.neverAsked: symptoms, reasons or results are never asked or typed in the AI chat

stop.words: trouble breathing, won't wake up, blue lips, or a seizure
stop.say: Call 911 now. Rosie can't book care for an emergency.
stop.booking: no booking; the same words in a later text get 911 again, and any visit stays booked

stop.say: Call Poison Help now at 1-800-222-1222. If the child isn't breathing or won't wake up, call 911.

nurseLine.words: the office's own list of signs for its nurse line (the example office lists a fever in a baby under 3 months)
nurseLine.say: Please call the office's nurse line now: (555) 010-0177, option 2. If it's an emergency, call 911.
nurseLine.booking: no booking by the AI until the nurse has talked with the parent

goOn.words: a sick child with nothing on the lists above
goOn.what: matched to the office's own sick visit; Rosie never judges how sick a child is

pf.safety.always: the general screen: danger to life, fire, gas or a medical emergency gets 911, and words about self-harm get 988

steps.result: covered, some services only, not covered, or can't check now (the desk checks later, and the family may cancel free)

pf.first_steps.prep: arrive 10 minutes early; bring the plan card, and the vaccine record if it isn't on file; a parent or guardian comes with the child, or an adult the parent named with a signed OK; at home: the baby's last weight from the hospital, if you have it

pf.visit.checkIn: at the office: the check-in code at the front desk, and the desk checks the adult is the parent or guardian, or the adult the parent named; a video visit: the code read out at the start; at home: the code from the parent at the door
pf.visit.beforeWork: the nurse checks the child's weight and height and the changes since the last visit, before the exam
pf.visit.changes: the clinician picks the shots due at the visit, from the child's age and record; a test is added only with the parent's yes, with any self-pay price first; more care is booked as its own visit only if the parent asks
pf.visit.done: the check-in code or DONE; the visit notes, results and vaccine record stay in the office's own records, never in Rosie or a text; the next well-child visit is booked at checkout
pf.visit.away: at home: the nurse practitioner brings a baby scale; a parent or guardian is there for the whole visit
pf.visit.childLeft: never: the adult who brought the child stays for the whole visit

pf.money.before: nothing taken at booking (the office bills the child's plan); a card saved only where the office turns on its no-show fee, never for a fee-free family; shots are never paid up front; at home: nothing taken
pf.money.plans: the plans the office takes (its own list); the front desk checks each plan by hand and records it; the share is an estimate, not a promise
pf.money.selfPay: a self-pay family is told while booking that they can get a written price estimate, and gets it on time; a bill far above it can be disputed (the federal rules set how)
pf.money.vaccines: shots are never paid up front; a child in the state's free vaccine program is never turned away for not paying the shot fee, and any shot fee stays within the program's limit (a switch from the state's form)
pf.money.fees: the no-show fee: $20 at the example office, only when the owner confirms it; the same fee for every family who may be charged one
pf.money.feeFree: a switch: no fee ever for families whose plan or the state's rules bar one (like Medicaid, where that applies), or whom the owner marks fee-free; their texts say 'No fee to cancel or miss'
pf.money.after: at the office: any share at the front desk, the office's own way; a balance after the plan pays is billed by the office, not by Rosie's text; a video visit's share is taken by the front desk its own way; at home: the office bills the plan its own way, or Rosie texts a self-pay family the bill after DONE
pf.money.private: a teen's private visit: how it's billed is the office's switch, so no plan statement reaches a parent; Rosie sends no bill or receipt about it to anyone but the teen
pf.money.rosfield: the $2 per booking applies to this work, as to every kind of work (D97): a flat fee for each booking Rosie's AI makes, shown at sign-up for the owner's yes; a booking the business puts in itself carries no $2; card payments cost only Stripe's own card fee, paid to Stripe
pf.money.caps: deposit cap: from the state form (no deposits are taken); fee limits for plan patients: from the plan's and the state's rules

pf.messages.never: texts carry only the practice's name, the date, the time, the address and a secure link: never the visit type, the reason, symptoms, shots, results or the clinician's name (at a home visit the clinician's name stays, for the door check)
pf.messages.staff: texts to the owner and staff carry no health detail either: the child's initials, the time and a link; the visit type and any notes about the child are on the secure page
pf.messages.languages: English and Spanish; the secure page asks if the family needs an interpreter, and the office is told
pf.messages.minors: texts go to the parent or guardian; a teen's private visit is texted only to the teen's own phone, with no visit type, and never shows on a parent's list or in the family's texts; a child under 13 never texts Rosie, and nothing about them is kept
pf.messages.medical: a medical question is never answered, saved or passed on: 911 if it's an emergency, then the nurse line or the patient portal

pf.staff.licenses: each pediatrician's, nurse practitioner's, physician assistant's and nurse's own license, per state
pf.staff.skills: pediatricians and nurse practitioners: well-child visits, sick visits, new families, video visits and newborn home visits; nurses: flu shots and shot-only visits on the clinician's order; the lactation consultant: breastfeeding help; only people cleared for home visits go to homes
pf.staff.supervision: a nurse practitioner or physician assistant works within the state's rules for supervision or a collaboration agreement (a switch from the state's form)
pf.staff.oks: the owner OKs a new family's first visit, same-day times for a new family, and anything a nurse flags
pf.staff.standIn: a pediatrician out: the nurse practitioner may take the visit, with the parent's yes; nobody is moved without it
pf.staff.away: the home visit team is the people cleared for home visits, with a baby scale

pf.rules.records: a child's records are kept by the office as long as the state's rules require (a child's records may be kept longer); a delete request removes only Rosie's own booking details, never the office's records
pf.rules.copies: a parent's copy of the child's records within the time the rules set; Rosie sends only booking and payment records
pf.rules.showLicense: the license shown where the state asks: posted at the office, and on a visit away from it
pf.rules.minors: who may consent for a child, which visit types a teen may book alone, and from what age (a switch from the state form)
pf.rules.custody: either parent may book unless the office marks a limit it holds, like a court order; anyone else only if the family's record names them
pf.rules.language: free language help where the rules require it, like for practices that take Medicaid
pf.rules.host: a school physicals day only under the school's written OK and its sign-in rules (S1-58); the example sets none
pf.rules.ads: no free-visit or price claims the state's rules don't allow
pf.rules.privacy: health privacy rules for every message and form

pf.edges.lateArrival: up to 15 minutes late: still seen; later, the desk may offer a new time (the office decides; Rosie never changes the booking itself)
pf.edges.officeLate: when the office runs late, a new time costs nothing
pf.edges.standIn: a pediatrician out: the nurse practitioner, with the parent's yes, or new times with no fee
pf.edges.forms: a form not done by its due date: one reminder, then Sam keeps the visit (signed on the secure page at the front desk first), moves it, or cancels with no fee (A7-74, B7-61)
pf.edges.planChange: the plan check comes back not covered: self-pay, or a free cancel
pf.edges.twoBookings: a family with visits open for two children: Rosie asks which one before any change
pf.edges.worse: a child seems worse before the visit: the 911 or Poison Help words if they match, the nurse line if it's on the office's list; Rosie never judges it, and the visit stays booked
pf.edges.healthQuestion: a question about medicine or care before the visit: never answered by Rosie; 911 if it's an emergency, then the nurse line or the portal
pf.edges.siblings: a sibling added to a booking gets their own time with the same clinician
pf.edges.newborn: a newborn visit that can't happen as booked: the soonest open window comes first, with no fee, and the nurse line is named in the text
pf.edges.other: all other edge cases the generic way
pf.edges.urgent: no service is sent now and nobody is on call (S2-30, S2-31): a sick child gets the soonest same-day time; the danger words get 911

notes:
Refit Oct 27 (REDESIGN 2 master): old words ops dropped (the master now words each step and reads the plug-in); facts children, forms, planbill, video, extrawork; switch sensitive; no $2; amounts per path with name; own record rows say the plan is billed (pay.price, pay.left, pay.staff); the teen private visit is the master's A4-90 now; rename pairs re-pointed to today's master words (no clinician name in office texts; no visit type in owner texts).
From: dentist, the clinic pilot. A pediatric office runs the same way: visits of a set length booked with a clinician by name, health forms only on the secure page, the front desk checks each plan by hand, nothing taken at booking, and no $2 for a health practice. What the dentist lacked is added: a parent or guardian books every child, who may bring a child is a switch, a teen's private visit (own branch on A4-24), the nurse line for urgent signs, same-day sick times, the well-child schedule, and shots never paid up front.
Names: Sam Lee, a pediatrician, owns Lee Newborn Care LLC (the master's main company: newborn care and breastfeeding help, at families' homes, 410 Main St) and Lee Family Pediatrics LLC (the second company: the office, 215 Alder St). Alex M. is the parent. Flow A: Mia, 4, a well-child visit Sat Oct 24, 11:00am with Nina. Flow B: baby Leo, born Sat Oct 17, a newborn home visit Thu Oct 22, arriving 8 to 10am, with Felix at 27 Spruce St.
People: Riley and Avery became Nina (pediatrician) and Elena (pediatric nurse practitioner) at the office; Jordan and Casey became Felix (nurse practitioner and lactation consultant) and Hugo (nurse practitioner) for home visits. Rosa, Marco and Hana are already names in the master, so they aren't used. A teen example is Ezra; the form example stays Grace V.
Kinds of work: plumbing became newborn care, electrical became breastfeeding help (it waits for Felix's lactation certification), the barbershop became the pediatric office. Licenses are switches from the state's form: each clinician's own license where the child is during the visit, the practice's registration where asked, a lactation certification, home-visit rules, the state vaccine program's enrollment, and supervision or collaboration for nurse practitioners.
Prices are the example offices' own, not a standard. Office self-pay: well-child visit $195, sick visit $140, video visit $140, flu shot $20, sports physical $40 ($45 from Nov 2), a new family's first visit $195, breastfeeding help at the office $120. At home: newborn home visit $179 ($199 when Sam goes), follow-up weight check $89, breastfeeding help $150. A plan pays its own fee. The master's $35 haircut isn't used: Mia's well-child visit is billed to her plan, with a $0 share in the example.
Money A: list|none|counter is the main path (the desk checks the plan; any share at the front desk). It also covers a sick visit's copay, shots, self-pay visits, and a video visit's share, which the desk takes its own way. list|card|counter is only where the office turns on its $20 no-show fee, never for a fee-free family. Left out: holds, deposits and full prepay (shots and visits are never prepaid), photos and visit pricing (every visit has its price), Rosfield's bill and the saved-card charge (a balance after the plan pays is the office's own bill).
Money B: list|none|own is the main path (the office bills the baby's plan its own way). list|none|bill is a family paying for itself: nothing taken, and Rosie texts the $179 bill when Felix texts DONE. Left out: cards, holds, deposits, full price, photos and visit pricing.
The sign-up's money words follow that (S1-12 to S1-18, S1-41 to S1-49, S1-57): nothing taken, no fee unless Sam turns one on, shots never prepaid, no tip line, cards only. S11-54 and S11-56 no longer give a service a hold or a price change it never uses.
Clocks: A books Wed Oct 21, 7:15 to 7:22pm, reminds Fri 10am, day list Sat 8am, check-in 11:00am (a 30-minute visit), rating 4pm. B books Mon Oct 19, 6:40 to 6:48pm, reminds Wed 10am, day list Thu 7am, OMW 8:05, check-in 8:20, DONE 9:20 (a 60-minute visit; B8-41 t), self-pay bill 9:22 (B9-06 t), receipt 9:25 (B10-01 t), rating 11am. Lee Newborn Care opens 7:30am, as B3-03 and B3-15 say. The visit-day what-ifs in section 7 (A7-14, A7-21, A7-29; B7-18, B7-27) keep the master's times: they come after the day list and before the visit, and each branch's own clock runs forward.
Texts: a customer text carries only the business, the date, the time and the place, never the visit type, shots or results. A's texts drop the clinician's name; B's keep it for the door check. Owner and staff texts carry the child's initials (M.M., L.M.) and a link, never the visit type or a health note (A6-15, A8-01, A8-38, B6-14, B8-01, S11-03, S11-04). Results only in person or in the office's patient portal.
Who may book: a parent or guardian, from the family's record; either parent unless the office holds a court order; anyone else only if the record names them (A4-24, A4-25). A teen alone only for visit types the office marks private, where the state's rules allow (own steps A4-x01, A4-x02). A child under 13 is asked for a grown-up and nothing is kept (A4-27). 'Another adult' is off (A4-24): every patient is a child.
Who may bring the child is a switch (pf.questions.whoMayBring): a parent, a guardian, or an adult the parent OKs on the secure page (A8-02, B4-27). The 'something required is missing' example is that parent's OK (A8-51 to A8-60).
Safety: the child's 911 words, Poison Help, and the office's nurse line, (555) 010-0177 option 2, for the signs on its own list (A3-22 to A3-26, A7-12, A7-13, B3-18 to B3-21, B4-82, B7-16, B7-17, B10-22). Rosie never judges how sick a child is, and the visit stays booked.
Stand-ins: nobody is moved to another clinician without the parent's yes (old flow pd20o), so Sam turns the no-reply default off: A7-21 and B7-22 hold the time and ask Sam to call.
